SCI // TRIVIAPART 2 · THE BIG REVEAL

All puzzles complete

Free will is a myth

At least, that’s what we’re going to question today. What if your brain knows something about your decisions that you don’t?

SCI // TRIVIAPART 3 · MEET THE SPLIT BRAIN

Two hemispheres, one brain

Two sides.
One connection.

The left and right hemispheres normally communicate through the corpus callosum, a thick bundle of nerve fibers.

For some people with severe epilepsy, surgeons have cut this connection to stop seizures spreading. The result is known as a split brain.

When the sides cannot communicate normally, they can sometimes respond to information independently.

↙
SCI // TRIVIAPART 4 · THE EXPERIMENT

The chicken claw and snow scene

Two pictures.
Two answers.

Researchers showed a chicken claw to one hemisphere and a snowy scene to the other. Then they asked the patient to choose matching pictures.

🐔chicken
🪏shovel

One hand chose a chicken. The other chose a shovel. Both choices fit what each side had seen.

SCI // TRIVIAPART 5 · THE BRAIN’S INTERPRETER

Are we making choices or explaining them?

Your brain
loves a story.

When asked to explain the chicken and shovel, the patient said the shovel was for cleaning the chicken shed. The speaking hemisphere had not seen the snow.

Scientists call this the left-brain interpreter: parts of the brain may create a logical explanation even without the full story.

That does not prove free will is fake. It shows our conscious explanation of a choice can be incomplete.

“The shovel is for the chicken shed!”
“Wait… did I know the real reason?”
SCI // TRIVIAPART 6 · THINK IT THROUGH

A question without a simple answer

🧠

Do we control
our brains, or do
our brains control us?

If your brain can give you an explanation that is not fully true, how certain can you be about why you make your decisions? And what does it mean for the idea of one unified self?

Thank you for listening.
